newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: German crude imports fall 2.5 percent in H1 1997.
newsitem.headline: German crude imports fall 2.5 percent in H1 1997.

text.p: German crude oil imports fell by 2.5 percent to 48.3 million tonnes in the first half of the year, the German economics agency (BAW) said on Friday.
At the same time, the cost of imports rose by 1.3 billion marks to 12.1 billion marks as the price per tonne rose 14.8 percent to 250.12 marks.
In June alone, crude imports were down 15.0 percent year-on-year to 7.0 million tonnes. The average price rose by 7.7 percent to 230.47 marks per tonne.
The first half fall follows last October's merger of the Karlsruhe refinery activities of Esso and OMW and the resultant cut of some 3.4 million tonnes of annual capacity.
June's drop came during the shutdown and upgrade of the Wilhelmshaven refinery in northern Germany.
Traders said the high price of crude in German marks also discouraged some from buying. In June, the dollar was almost 15 percent higher against the mark than a year ago.
While German crude imports fell in the first half of this year, upgrades and one new refinery in 1997 mean they are likely to rise next year, the German oil industry association said.
Some analysts have said healthier 1996 margins have stalled further closure plans and encouraged upgrades.
The capacity of the Wilhelmshaven refinery, owned by the Hamburg-based part of Louis Dreyfus has expanded by about 35,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 210,000 bpd.
The Holborn refinery in Hamburg has added about another 15,000 bpd.
In eastern Germany, the Leunawerke refinery closed at the end of June, but the autumn opening of the 175,000 bpd Leuna 2000 refinery will lead to a net gain of about 70,000 bpd.
